title: Reject an unknown level from inside a switch expression

blocks.text: Since Java 14 a `switch` expression may use `throw` as the body of a case, which makes rejecting an unexpected value a one-liner. Write `LevelParser.parseLevel(String s)` as a single `switch` expression:

A message should say what was wrong *and with which value*. Every input that is not a known level, whatever it is, gets the same exception; remember what a plain `switch` does with `null`, and that Java 21 lets a case say otherwise.

cases.says: "low" is 1 and "high" is 3, and an unknown level throws IllegalArgumentException.
The message states the rejected value: "Unknown level: mid", not a bare "Unknown level".
null gets the same IllegalArgumentException, not the NullPointerException a plain switch on null throws.

concepts: A message states what was wrong and with which value.
A switch expression can use throw as the body of a case to reject an unexpected value.
